searchDocs.title: GiveBadge​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> BadgeGiver:GiveBadge( player: Player ,-- The player to award the badge to. badgeId: number,-- The ID of the badge to award. spreadSeconds: number?-- Longest random delay before the award is attempted. ) → () Queues the specified badge to be awarded to the player, unless their data shows they already have it. Returns once the badge is queued, not once it is awarded. spreadSeconds delays the award by a random time up to that many seconds. Useful when many players earn a badge at the same moment, so their requests reach BadgeService over time rather than all at once.

searchDocs.keywords: roblox badges badgeservice gamebeast roblox analytics

searchDocs.title: Badges​
searchDocs.content: BadgeGiver awards badges from the server. It queues awards so they stay inside BadgeService's request limits, and records each award in player data so a badge that fails is tried again later.  local BadgeGiver = shared("BadgeGiver") BadgeGiver:GiveBadge(player, 123456789)   GiveBadge(player, badgeId, spreadSeconds?) returns once the badge is queued, not once it is awarded. It yields until the player's data loads. It does nothing if the player's data shows they already have the badge, or if the player has left.  When many players earn a badge at the same moment, such as at the end of a round, pass spreadSeconds to delay each award by a random time up to that many seconds. Their requests then reach BadgeService over time rather than all at once:  for _, player in winners do BadgeGiver:GiveBadge(player, ROUND_WINNER_BADGE_ID, 10) end   note In Studio, GiveBadge does nothing, since badges can't be awarded there.

searchDocs.title: How awards are processed​
searchDocs.content: GiveBadge adds the badge to the player's PendingBadges, then queues it. Queuing the same badge twice for one player does nothing.A worker takes awards from the queue. It first checks UserHasBadgeAsync, and only calls AwardBadgeAsync if the player doesn't have the badge.On success, the badge moves from PendingBadges to AwardedBadges. If BadgeService says the badge can't be awarded, for example because it's disabled, the server warns and the badge is removed from PendingBadges without being retried.If a request errors, the award is retried with a delay that doubles from 2 seconds up to 60, with jitter. After 5 failed attempts it stops for the session.When a player joins, every badge left in their PendingBadges is queued again. This covers awards that failed, and awards cut short by the player leaving.  Badge IDs are saved as string keys, so AwardedBadges and PendingBadges look like { ["123456789"] = true }. Keep both keys in the profile template.

searchDocs.title: Request limits​
searchDocs.content: BadgeService allows 50 + 35 × players requests per minute across the server. The queue uses at most 80% of that, which leaves room for other scripts. When the budget for the last minute is spent, awards wait.  If 5 requests fail in a row, the queue pauses for 60 seconds and warns. This stops it from adding load while BadgeService is having trouble.

searchDocs.title: Analytics​
searchDocs.content: Order sets up the Gamebeast SDK on the server and the client. It's installed as the GamebeastSDK package.

searchDocs.title: Enabling Gamebeast​
searchDocs.content: The server reads its Gamebeast key from an experience secret named Gamebeast, using HttpService:GetSecret("Gamebeast"). Add the secret in your experience's settings on the Creator Hub, with your Gamebeast project's SDK key as its value.  With the secret, AnalyticsServer sets up the SDK when the server starts.Without it, the server prints that Gamebeast analytics is disabled, and doesn't set up the SDK.  Either way, the server sets the GamebeastEnabled attribute on workspace to true or false. AnalyticsClient waits for that attribute, and only sets up the client SDK when it's true, since the client SDK waits for remotes that the server only creates during setup.

searchDocs.title: Sending events​
searchDocs.content: Order doesn't wrap the SDK, so use it directly through shared("GamebeastSDK"). For example, to send a marker from the server:  local GamebeastSDK = shared("GamebeastSDK") GamebeastSDK:GetService("Markers"):SendMarker("ItemPurchased", { ItemId = itemId, Price = price, })   See the Gamebeast Roblox SDK reference for the SDK's services, including markers, configs and experiments. If your game sells developer products, Gamebeast recommends tracking them with SendNewPurchaseGrantedMarker. On the client, check that workspace:GetAttribute("GamebeastEnabled") is true before using the SDK, because it won't be set up otherwise.

searchDocs.title: OnEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> Remote:OnEvent( callback: function,-- The callback to invoke when the event fires rateLimitInterval: number?,-- If provided, rate-limits the callback to this interval in seconds getRateLimitKey: RateLimitKeyGetter?-- If provided, rate-limits each key it returns separately ) → RemoteConnection-- A handle that disconnects the callback, safe to give to a Maid Connects the provided callback to the remote's event. Context is determined automatically. If a rateLimitInterval is provided, events fired within that duration will be queued and only the latest arguments processed. This can prevent remote spam, but may cause events to be dropped if set too high. OnServerEvent and OnClientEvent are aliases for this method. getRateLimitKey receives the event's arguments and returns a key. Each key is rate limited separately, so a remote whose payload names what it acts on (a setting, an item) keeps the latest event for each name rather than only the latest event overall. SettingRemote:OnEvent(function(player, settingName, value) -- ... end, 0.5, function(player, settingName) return settingName end)

searchDocs.title: Destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Remote:Destroy() → () Tears the remote down for good. It is removed from the registry, and on the server its instances are destroyed, which disconnects every client's listeners as well. Use this for remotes named after something that goes away, such as a per-round or per-object remote, so they do not build up. Any later call on this object does nothing. Calling GetRemote with the same name afterwards creates a new remote.

searchDocs.title: Rules​
searchDocs.content: Style - Contributions should do their best to conform to the Roblox Luau Style Guide. I realize that that's not always possible or practical, so some exceptions can be made in the interest of functionality.Utility - Contributions should expand or enhance Order in a way that aligns with the project's design philosophy of making things simpler and easier for the developer. Anything that does not do so will be rejected.Documentation - Any changes that add complex functionality should contain comments that explain why you're doing what you're doing. This is also part of the Roblox Luau Style Guide (rule #1), but is worth reiterating.

Change how they appear in DeveloperToolsConfig (src/client/core/lib/DeveloperTools):  Setting	Default	EffectChatCommands	true	Adds the /cmdr, /console and /branches chat commands. On touch devices, chat is the only way to open the tools without the top bar buttons. TopbarButtons	true	Adds top bar buttons for the tools. GroupTopbarButtons	true	When a player can see more than one tool button, puts them in a single "Dev" group that expands when selected.  Teleport requests from the Branches pane are checked on the server: only players with the branches permission are teleported, and only to places in the same experience.

searchDocs.title: Cmdr​
searchDocs.content: Cmdr's built-in commands are registered, including ban and unban, which accept a player in the server, an offline username, or #UserId. Players with the mod permission can run kick, boot, ban and unban. Every other command needs the cmdr permission.  Custom commands, types and hooks go in the CustomCommands, CustomTypes and CustomHooks folders under src/server/core/tasks/CmdrHooks. Order adds two types:  Type	Accepts	Parses tobranch	The name of a place in the experience	The place userIdOrPlayer / userIdsOrPlayers	A player in the server (with autocomplete), a UserId, or . / me for yourself	A UserId

searchDocs.title: Permissions​
searchDocs.content: Permissions are set in PermissionsConfig (src/shared/core/lib). A check takes the first rule that applies, in this order:  A runtime grant or revoke from PermissionService:SetRuntimePermission()UserDeniedPermissionsAdmins, then the test player and Studio settingsUserPermissionsGroupPermissions  GroupPermissions = { ["cmdr"] = { [123456] = { RoleIds = { 987654321 } }, }, },   Group permissions match role IDs, which you can copy with the "Copy Role ID" button at the bottom of a role's settings page. Roblox no longer uses rank to order roles, so it recommends checking role IDs instead. A MinimumRank rule still works but logs a deprecation warning. Only public roles can be checked.  Function	UsePermissionService:HasPermission(player, label)	Checks a player in the server. Works on the client and the server. PermissionService:UserHasPermission(userId, label)	Checks any user, including ones not in the server. PermissionService:SetRuntimePermission(label, userId, granted)	Server only. Grants (true) or revokes (false) a permission until the server shuts down, or removes the override (nil). Players in the server see the change through an attribute.

searchDocs.title: Installation​
searchDocs.content: RojoRoblox Package 1) Download VS Code and Rojo​ Download and install VS Code from hereFrom VS Code, install the extension Rojo from the Extensions tab on the left sidebar or through this link.In Roblox Studio, search for and add the plugin for Rojo through the toolbox, or use this link. 2) Create a new repository based on this template​ At the top of this page, click the green "Use this template" button and select "Create a new repository"Select the proper owner, add a name, choose your desired visiblity options, and click "Create repository from template"Using the software of your choice (I typically use VS Code's Source Control menu), clone your new repository to your computer 3) Install packages​ Order supports two package managers. Forest is recommended, and Wally is still supported. Forest (recommended)Wally Install Rokit, then run rokit install in your project's directory. This installs Rojo, StyLua and the Forest CLI at the versions listed in rokit.toml.Run forest install. Forest reads forest.json, installs shared packages into Packages and server-only packages into ServerPackages.Commit forest-lock.json whenever it changes, so every machine installs the same versions. tip Use one package manager per project. Forest removes Wally's _Index folders the next time it installs, and forest init --project converts an existing wally.toml into a forest.json. 4) Project configuration​ Open the new repository in VS Code and then open the default.project.json fileAt the top, you'll see a string that reads "New Order Project", replace this with the name of your new project and save the file 5) Sync code into Roblox Studio​ In VS Code, click the Rojo button on the bottom right (if you don't see this icon, verify the Rojo extension is installed and restart VS Code)In the context menu that appears, click on default.project.json at the bottomIn Roblox Studio, create or open a place file that will host your new experienceSwitch to the Plugins tab, and select RojoIn the Rojo window that appears, click "Connect" You are now up and running with Order! Any code you write in VS Code will be synced into your new game whenever you save the file.

searchDocs.title: Creating your first task​
searchDocs.content: Tasks are the primary way to run code at runtime in Order. Any module placed inside a tasks folder will be automatically discovered and initialized by the framework.

searchDocs.title: 1) Create the task file​
searchDocs.content: Inside the appropriate context folder (client, server, or shared), create a tasks subfolder if one doesn't already exist, then add a new .luau file inside it. For example, to create a server-side task:  src/ server/ core/ tasks/ MyTask.luau ← your new task

searchDocs.title: 2) Write the task module​
searchDocs.content: A task is a regular Lua table returned by the module. Add :Prep() for synchronous setup that runs before everything else, and :Init() for your main async logic that runs after all prep work is done. Both are optional.  local PlayerUtils = shared("PlayerUtils") local MyTask = { Priority = 0, -- optional, higher values initialize first } function MyTask:Prep() -- Synchronous setup — runs before :Init() on any task. -- Safe to set up state here, but avoid yielding. self.Players = {} end function MyTask:Init() -- Async runtime logic — runs after all :Prep() calls finish. PlayerUtils:PlayerAdded(function(player) ... end) print("MyTask initialized!") end return MyTask

searchDocs.title: 3) Load other modules from your task​
searchDocs.content: Call shared() at the top of the file, before defining the task table, to load dependencies by name, partial path, or direct reference:  local PlayerData = shared("PlayerData") local GetRemote = shared("GetRemote") local MyTask = {} function MyTask:Init() GetRemote("Counter"):OnEvent(function(player) PlayerData:IncrementNumValue(player, "Counter", 1) end) end return MyTask   For modules involved in a cyclic dependency, you can still call shared() at the top level — but any code that actually uses the returned value must be inside a function:  local CyclicModule = shared("CyclicModule") -- fine at the top level local MyTask = {} function MyTask:Init() CyclicModule:DoThing() -- safe: accessed inside a function, not bare code end return MyTask   warning Bare top-level code that directly calls or indexes a cyclic dependency will not work. Order detects this and will skip initialization on that module with a warning.  Once the framework initializes, your task will be picked up automatically — no registration or additional wiring needed.

searchDocs.title: Special Notes
searchDocs.keywords: order cyclic dependencies luau require shared

searchDocs.title: No bare code in modules with cyclic dependencies​
searchDocs.content: In order to support cyclic dependencies, it must be guaranteed that the module in question has no bare code that references a cyclic dependency. That is to say that any code that references the cyclic dependency must be contained within a function. If Order detects this bare code, you will be notified with a warning in the output and no operation will be processed on the module in question.

searchDocs.title: Loading modules with non-unique names​
searchDocs.content: Modules can be specified through several different paths. If the name is unique, you can reference it simply through that. If two modules exist with the same name however, Order will warn you that it found two or more possible modules for your request, and will ask you to be more specific. You can use any level of the module paths it provides you with, as long as they're unique as well.  Order does not index all potential file paths by default, so it is recommended to use the shortest unique paths possible in order to conserve memory usage.

searchDocs.title: Printing module tables​
searchDocs.content: One of the complications with the method Order uses to support cyclic dependencies is that if you try to print out one of these module's tables, it would return a table address instead of an output-friendly table. In order to preserve as much functionality as possible, Order will list out table keys and values in a custom format when converting the table to a string.

searchDocs.title: Working with AtomicUI
searchDocs.keywords: roblox ui framework atomicui luau ui ui state manager

searchDocs.title: Creating a ScreenGui​
searchDocs.content: Use ScreenGui.new to create a container for your UI. It automatically parents to PlayerGui at runtime and to CoreGui in story environments.  local ScreenGui = shared("ScreenGui") ---@module ScreenGui local MyGui = ScreenGui.new("MyGui")

searchDocs.title: Creating an AtomicPane​
searchDocs.content: Subclass AtomicPane to build a custom UI component. Override _draw to update your elements each frame based on spring values.  local AtomicPane = shared("AtomicPane") ---@module AtomicPane local MyPane = setmetatable({}, AtomicPane) MyPane.__index = MyPane MyPane.ClassName = "MyPane" function MyPane:_draw() local alpha = self._springs.Alpha.Position self.Gui.Visible = alpha < 0.999 self.Gui.GroupTransparency = alpha end function MyPane.new(parent: Instance) local self = setmetatable(AtomicPane.new("MyPaneTemplate", { TitleLabel = "Title", }), MyPane) self:SetVisible(false, true) -- start hidden, no animation self.Gui.Parent = parent return self end return MyPane   The string key passed to AtomicPane.new must match the name of a GuiObject in ReplicatedStorage.GuiTemplates. The second argument maps descendant instance names to keys on self for quick access.

searchDocs.title: Automatic alpha mapping​
searchDocs.content: Instead of manually interpolating transparencies in _draw, call MapAlpha on any element whose transparency properties should be driven by the Alpha spring automatically:  function MyPane.new(parent: Instance) local self = setmetatable(AtomicPane.new("MyPaneTemplate", {}), MyPane) self:MapAlpha(self.Gui) -- maps all descendants recursively self:SetVisible(false, true) self.Gui.Parent = parent return self end   MapAlpha caches each element's current transparencies as its fully visible values, so map elements while they look the way they should when visible. Mapped values are drawn at the pane's current alpha as soon as they are mapped.  Pass a list of instances as the second argument to skip their subtrees, for example nested components that animate their own transparency:  self:MapAlpha(self.Gui, { self.LoadingSpinner })   To change mapping after the fact:  UnmapAlpha(element) stops driving an element and its descendants, and leaves their transparencies as they are.SetMappedAlpha(element, property, visibleAlpha) changes the value one property shows when the pane is fully visible, for elements whose resting look changes after they were mapped.

searchDocs.title: Custom springs​
searchDocs.content: Add extra springs for animations beyond visibility:  function MyPane.new(parent: Instance) local self = setmetatable(AtomicPane.new("MyPaneTemplate", {}), MyPane) self:AddSpring("Slide", { s = 35, d = 1, i = 0 }) self:SetVisible(false, true) self.Gui.Parent = parent return self end function MyPane:_draw() local alpha = self._springs.Alpha.Position local slide = self._springs.Slide.Position self.Gui.Visible = alpha < 0.999 self.Gui.Position = UDim2.new(slide * -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0) end

searchDocs.title: Creating an AtomicButton​
searchDocs.content: Subclass AtomicButton the same way as AtomicPane. It adds Hovered, Pressed, Selected, and Enabled springs automatically, along with the corresponding signals and setter methods.  local AtomicButton = shared("AtomicButton") ---@module AtomicButton local MyButton = setmetatable({}, AtomicButton) MyButton.__index = MyButton MyButton.ClassName = "MyButton" function MyButton:_draw() local alpha = self._springs.Alpha.Position local hovered = self._springs.Hovered.Position local pressed = self._springs.Pressed.Position self.Gui.Visible = alpha < 0.999 -- Subtle scale feedback local scale = 1 - pressed * 0.04 + hovered * 0.02 self.Gui.Size = UDim2.fromScale(scale, scale) end function MyButton.new(parent: Instance) local self = setmetatable(AtomicButton.new("MyButtonTemplate", {}), MyButton) self.Activated:Connect(function() print("Button clicked!") end) self:SetVisible(false, true) self.Gui.Parent = parent return self end return MyButton   note AtomicButton automatically creates a transparent TextButton named Sensor as a child of Gui if one does not already exist. You do not need to add one manually. GetSensor() returns it, which is useful for gamepad navigation since selection lands on the sensor rather than the pane's Gui.

searchDocs.title: Linking panes​
searchDocs.content: Use AtomicPane:Link to tie the lifetime (and optionally visibility) of a child pane to a parent pane. When the parent is destroyed, the linked child is cleaned up automatically.  local childPane = MyChildPane.new() childPane:Link(parentPane) -- Also mirror visibility changes: childPane:Link(parentPane, true)

searchDocs.title: Using UIStateManager​
searchDocs.content: UIStateManager allows you to define named application states that show and hide groups of registered UI components together.

searchDocs.title: Registering a component​
searchDocs.content: Call RegisterComponent with a unique name and the pane instance. The component must implement :Show() and :Hide(), which all AtomicPane subclasses provide.  local UIStateManager = shared("UIStateManager") ---@module UIStateManager UIStateManager:RegisterComponent("HUD", myHudPane) UIStateManager:RegisterComponent("PauseMenu", myPausePane)

searchDocs.title: Registering states​
searchDocs.content: Define states with RegisterState, specifying which components to show and hide:  UIStateManager:RegisterState("Gameplay", { Shows = { "HUD" }, Hides = { "PauseMenu" }, CoreGui = { Shows = { "*" }, Hides = {}, }, GamepadCursorEnabled = false, }) UIStateManager:RegisterState("Paused", { Shows = { "PauseMenu" }, Hides = { "HUD" }, GamepadCursorEnabled = true, })   Use "*" in Shows or Hides to target all registered components at once.

searchDocs.title: Switching states​
searchDocs.content: UIStateManager:SetState("Paused") -- Restore the previous state UIStateManager:PreviousState() -- Return to the default state UIStateManager:SetDefault()

searchDocs.title: Blocking transitions​
searchDocs.content: Add a Blocks list to a state's properties to prevent certain transitions while that state is active:  UIStateManager:RegisterState("Cutscene", { Shows = {}, Hides = { "*" }, Blocks = { "*" }, -- prevent all state changes })   Pass true as the second argument to SetState to force a transition regardless of blocks:  UIStateManager:SetState("Gameplay", true)

searchDocs.title: Reacting to state changes​
searchDocs.content: Use RegisterEventHook to run logic whenever the state changes:  UIStateManager:RegisterEventHook("StateChange", function(newState, oldState) print("Transitioned from", oldState, "to", newState) end)   Available hooks: StateChange, BeforeStateChange, AfterStateChange, CoreGuiChange.

searchDocs.title: Networking with GetRemote
searchDocs.keywords: roblox remotes remoteevent remotefunction getremote luau networking

searchDocs.title: Server → Client​
searchDocs.content: -- Fire to one player MyRemote:FireClient(player, "Hello!") -- Fire to a list of players MyRemote:FireClientList({ player1, player2 }, "Hello!") -- Fire to all players MyRemote:FireAllClients("Hello, everyone!") -- Fire to all players except one, or except a list of players MyRemote:FireAllExcept(player, "Everyone but you!") MyRemote:FireAllExcept({ player1, player2 }, "Everyone but you two!")

searchDocs.title: Client → Server​
searchDocs.content: MyRemote:FireServer("Hello, server!")

searchDocs.title: Context-agnostic firing​
searchDocs.content: :Fire() routes automatically — it calls :FireServer() from the client or :FireAllClients() from the server:  MyRemote:Fire("Hello!")

searchDocs.title: Listening for events​
searchDocs.content: :OnEvent() also routes automatically — it connects to OnServerEvent on the server and OnClientEvent on the client. The server callback receives the firing player as the first argument.  -- Server MyRemote:OnEvent(function(player, message) print(player.Name, "says:", message) end) -- Client MyRemote:OnEvent(function(message) print("Server says:", message) end)   OnServerEvent and OnClientEvent are aliases for :OnEvent() and can be used for clarity.  :OnEvent() returns a connection. Disconnect it, or give it to a Maid, when the listener should stop before the session ends:  self.Maid:GiveTask(MyRemote:OnEvent(function(message) print(message) end))

searchDocs.title: Rate limiting​
searchDocs.content: Pass a rateLimitInterval (in seconds) as the second argument to avoid processing bursts of events. Only the latest arguments received within the interval will be processed:  MyRemote:OnEvent(function(player, value) -- processes at most once per 0.1 seconds per callback updateHealthBar(value) end, 0.1)   caution Rate limiting drops intermediate events — only the most recent arguments within the interval are kept. Avoid this for events where every individual fire must be processed.  By default, each player shares one rate limit for the callback. To limit separate streams independently, pass a function as the third argument that returns a key for each event. Events with different keys are limited separately:  -- Each unit a player controls is limited on its own MyRemote:OnEvent(function(player, unitId, position) moveUnit(player, unitId, position) end, 0.1, function(player, unitId) return unitId end)

searchDocs.title: Unreliable events​
searchDocs.content: For high-frequency data where occasional packet loss is acceptable (e.g. position updates, visual effects), use the unreliable variants. These use UnreliableRemoteEvent under the hood and have lower overhead.  -- Server → Client MyRemote:FireClientUnreliable(player, position) MyRemote:FireAllClientsUnreliable(position) -- Client → Server MyRemote:FireServerUnreliable(position) -- Context-agnostic MyRemote:FireUnreliable(position) -- Listening MyRemote:OnUnreliableEvent(function(player, position) updateMarker(player, position) end)   FireClientFast, FireServerFast, FireFast, and OnServerUnreliableEvent/OnClientUnreliableEvent are all aliases for their unreliable counterparts.

searchDocs.title: Remote functions (invoke/callback)​
searchDocs.content: Use OnInvoke to register a handler and :Invoke() or :InvokeServer() / :InvokeClient() to call it and wait for a return value.

searchDocs.title: Client invokes the server​
searchDocs.content: -- Server — register the handler MyRemote:OnInvoke(function(player, request) if request == "getData" then return { score = 100 } end end) -- Client — invoke and await result local data = MyRemote:InvokeServer("getData") print(data.score) --> 100

searchDocs.title: Server invokes a client​
searchDocs.content: -- Client — register the handler MyRemote:OnInvoke(function(request) return UserInputService:GetLastInputType().Name end) -- Server — invoke a specific player and await result local inputType = MyRemote:InvokeClient(player, "getInput")

searchDocs.title: Context-agnostic invoke​
searchDocs.content: :Invoke() routes automatically. When called from the client it invokes the server; when called from the server the first argument must be the target Player:  -- From client local result = MyRemote:Invoke("getData") -- From server local result = MyRemote:Invoke(player, "getData")   caution Invoking a client from the server can hang indefinitely if the client disconnects or never responds. Prefer firing events with a follow-up callback pattern for server-initiated requests where possible.

searchDocs.title: Dedicated remote per feature​
searchDocs.content: Create one remote per logical feature rather than multiplexing many actions over a single remote. This keeps handlers focused and makes debugging easier.  -- inventory.server.luau local InventoryRemote = GetRemote("Inventory") InventoryRemote:OnEvent(function(player, action, itemId) if action == "equip" then equipItem(player, itemId) elseif action == "drop" then dropItem(player, itemId) end end)

searchDocs.title: Validating client input on the server​
searchDocs.content: Never trust data sent from the client. Always validate before acting on it:  InventoryRemote:OnEvent(function(player, action, itemId) if typeof(itemId) ~= "number" then return end if not playerOwnsItem(player, itemId) then return end equipItem(player, itemId) end)

searchDocs.title: Sharing the remote reference​
searchDocs.content: Since GetRemote returns the same object for a given name everywhere, you can safely call it in both a server script and a client script using the same name string — no shared module or passing of references is needed.  -- myFeature.server.luau local MyRemote = GetRemote("MyFeature") -- myFeature.client.luau local MyRemote = GetRemote("MyFeature") -- same underlying remote

searchDocs.title: Destroying a remote​
searchDocs.content: :Destroy() disconnects every listener, removes the remote instances on the server, and turns the remote's methods into no-ops. Use it for remotes created for something temporary, such as a single round:  local RoundRemote = GetRemote(`Round:{roundId}`) -- When the round ends RoundRemote:Destroy()

searchDocs.title: StateManager
searchDocs.keywords: roblox state machine statemanager luau gameplay states

searchDocs.title: Defining states​
searchDocs.content: States are defined in GlobalConfig (src/shared/core/lib/StateManager/Configs/GlobalConfig.luau). Each key is a state name, and every rule is optional:  return { Sprinting = { BlockedBy = { "Stunned" }, Deactivates = { "Crouching" }, Tags = { "Movement" }, }, Crouching = { BlockedBy = { "Stunned" }, Deactivates = { "Sprinting" }, Tags = { "Movement" }, }, Stunned = { Deactivates = { "Sprinting", "Crouching" }, }, InMenu = { Activates = { "MouseUnlocked" }, }, MouseUnlocked = {}, } :: StateConfig   Rule	Effect when the state is activatedBlockedBy	Fails if any of these states is active. Deactivates	Deactivates any of these states that are active. Activates	Also activates these states, following their own rules. Tags	Groups the state so it can be checked or changed with others. See Tags.  The config also has a Requires rule, but it doesn't work yet: a state with Requires set can never be activated.  shared("StateManager") returns one shared manager built from GlobalConfig. Every state the code refers to must be in the config. Activating a state that isn't there raises an error.

searchDocs.title: Activating and deactivating​
searchDocs.content: local StateManager = shared("StateManager") local activated, blockingState = StateManager:ActivateState("Sprinting") if not activated then print(`Can't sprint while {blockingState.Name} is active`) end StateManager:DeactivateState("Sprinting") StateManager:ToggleState("Crouching")   ActivateState returns true and the state if it is now active (or already was). It returns false and the active state that blocked it otherwise. States listed in Deactivates never block, they're turned off instead.  Function	UseActivateState(name)	Activates a state if its rules allow it. DeactivateState(name)	Deactivates a state. ToggleState(name)	Activates or deactivates a state, depending on whether it's active. IsStateActive(name)	Whether a state is active. Pass a list to check that all of them are active. IsAnyStateActive(names)	Whether any state in the list is active. IsStateActivatable(name)	Whether ActivateState would succeed right now, and the name of the blocking state if not. GetState(name)	Returns the State object. GetActiveStates() / GetAllStates()	Returns the active states or all states, keyed by name. These are the manager's own tables, so don't change them.

searchDocs.title: Reacting to changes​
searchDocs.content: The manager has StateActivated and StateDeactivated signals, which fire with the state's name:  StateManager.StateActivated:Connect(function(stateName) print(`{stateName} on`) end)   To react to one state, use its own signals, or bind a handler that runs on both activation and deactivation:  StateManager:GetStateActivatedSignal("InMenu"):Connect(function() print("Menu opened") end) local sprinting = StateManager:GetState("Sprinting") sprinting:BindHandler(function(state) humanoid.WalkSpeed = if state:IsActive() then 24 else 16 end, "SprintSpeed")   State member	UseName	The state's name. IsActive()	Whether the state is active. Activated / Deactivated	Signals for this state. BindHandler(handler, handlerName?)	Calls handler(state) on every activation and deactivation, in a new thread. Returns the handler's name, a generated one if you didn't pass one. UnbindHandler(handlerName) / ClearHandlers()	Removes one handler or all of them. LastActivatedAt / LastDeactivatedAt	os.clock() time of the last change.

searchDocs.title: Tags​
searchDocs.content: Tags act on groups of states:  -- End all movement states except crouching StateManager:DeactivateStatesWithTagExcept("Movement", "Crouching") local activeMovementStates = StateManager:GetStatesActiveWithTag("Movement")   Function	UseGetStatesActiveWithTag(tag)	Returns the active states with the tag. ActivateStatesWithTag(tag)	Tries to activate every state with the tag. Returns whether any failed, then the activated and failed states. ActivateStatesWithTagExcept(tag, names)	The same, skipping one name or a list of names. Returns whether all succeeded, then the activated and failed states. DeactivateStatesWithTag(tag)	Deactivates every state with the tag. DeactivateStatesWithTagExcept(tag, names)	The same, skipping one name or a list of names.  caution The first value from ActivateStatesWithTag is true when something failed, but the first value from ActivateStatesWithTagExcept is true when everything succeeded.  Using a tag that no state has warns and changes nothing.

searchDocs.title: Player Data
searchDocs.keywords: roblox player data profilestore replicaservice datastore luau

searchDocs.title: The profile template​
searchDocs.content: ProfileTemplate (src/shared/core/lib/PlayerData/ProfileTemplate.luau) is the shape and starting value of every player's data. Add the keys your game needs:  local ProfileTemplate = { AwardedBadges = {}, PendingBadges = {}, Coins = 0, Settings = { MusicVolume = 0.5, }, }   New players start with a copy of the template.When a returning player loads, keys added to the template since they last played are filled in with their template values. Keys removed from the template stay in saved data until you clear them.The template is frozen, so code can't change it by accident.AwardedBadges and PendingBadges are used by BadgeGiver. Keep them.  Because the template is shared, the client can read it too. In Edit mode, where no server is running, DataController returns the template so UI previews have data to show.

searchDocs.title: Loading​
searchDocs.content: Data loads automatically when a player joins. Wait for it before using it:  local PlayerData = shared("PlayerData") Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player) if not PlayerData:WaitForData(player) then return -- The player left, or their data failed to load end print(PlayerData:GetValue(player, "Coins")) end)   WaitForData returns false if the player leaves or their data can't load. In a live server, a player whose data can't load is kicked with a message to try again. Studio doesn't kick, so you can still test.  A profile can only be loaded in one server at a time. When a player rejoins the same server quickly, their new load waits up to 15 seconds for the previous session to finish saving.

searchDocs.title: Reading and writing on the server​
searchDocs.content: Every function that takes a key path accepts a single key, a dot-separated path, or an array of keys:  PlayerData:GetValue(player, "Coins") PlayerData:GetValue(player, "Settings.MusicVolume") PlayerData:GetValue(player, { "Settings", "MusicVolume" })   Function	UseGetValue(player, keyPath)	Returns the value at the path, or nil if the last key is missing. Every table before the last key must exist, or it errors. SetValue(player, keyPath, value)	Sets the value and replicates it to the player. IncrementNumValue(player, keyPath, amount)	Adds a non-zero amount to a number (a missing value counts as 0) and returns the new value. Returns nil if the amount is 0 or the stored value isn't a number. Observe(player, keyPath, callback)	Calls callback(newValue, oldValue) with the current value right away, then on every change. Returns a connection. SetValueCallback(player, keyPath, callback, runImmediately?)	Like Observe, but only calls back for the current value when runImmediately is true. GetPlayerDataReplica(player)	Returns the player's Replica. Yields until data loads, and returns nil if the player leaves or their data can't load.  Each of these yields until the player's data loads. If the data can't load, they warn and return nil instead of acting. There's no warning if the player has already left.  caution Never change tables from GetValue in place. The change isn't replicated, and the client's copy goes out of date. For a single value, use SetValue. For arrays, use the replica's methods, such as ArrayInsert and ArrayRemove (see the Replica API): local replica = PlayerData:GetPlayerDataReplica(player) replica:ArrayInsert("OwnedItems", "Sword")

searchDocs.title: Reading on the client​
searchDocs.content: DataController mirrors the reading half of the server API, without the player argument:  local DataController = shared("DataController") local coinsConnection = DataController:Observe("Coins", function(coins) CoinsLabel.Text = `{coins}` end)   Function	UseGetValue(keyPath)	Returns the value at the path, or nil if any part of the path is missing. Yields until data arrives. Observe(keyPath, callback)	Calls back with the current value right away, then on every change. Returns a connection. SetValueCallback(keyPath, callback, runImmediately?)	Like Observe, but only calls back for the current value when runImmediately is true. GetData()	Returns the whole data table. Yields until data arrives. GetDataReplica()	Returns the Replica. Yields until it arrives.  Client data is read-only. To change data, send a request to the server with a remote and validate it there.

searchDocs.title: Saving​
searchDocs.content: ProfileStore saves each profile every few minutes and when the player leaves. To save sooner, for example after a purchase, call RequestSave:  PlayerData:IncrementNumValue(player, "Coins", 500) PlayerData:RequestSave(player)   RequestSave returns right away. It retries up to 3 times in the background and warns if every attempt fails. It returns false when there's nothing to save, such as when the player has left or data is read-only.

searchDocs.title: Profile holds​
searchDocs.content: When a player leaves, their profile is saved and released. If you have async work that still needs to write to their data, such as a purchase being processed, hold the profile until it finishes:  local holdId = PlayerData:CreateProfileHold(player) -- Async work that writes to the player's data PlayerData:ReleaseProfileHold(holdId)   CreateProfileHold returns nil if the player's profile isn't loaded, so create the hold before the work starts. When the player leaves, the release waits up to about 10 seconds for holds to clear, then releases the profile anyway.

searchDocs.title: Reading another player's data​
searchDocs.content: ViewProfileAsync(userId) returns a copy of any user's saved data, including users who aren't in the server. It returns nil if they have nothing saved or the read fails. It doesn't lock the profile, so it won't disturb a session they have in another server. Changes to the copy aren't saved.  local savedData = PlayerData:ViewProfileAsync(userId) if savedData then print(savedData.Coins) end

searchDocs.title: Data stores and testing​
searchDocs.content: Production places save to the PlayerData_Prod store. Testing places and Studio share one testing store, so testing never touches real player data. See Environments to set a place's environment.  Two attributes on workspace change how data is handled while testing:  Attribute	EffectUseMockData	Uses an in-memory store that is discarded when the server closes. ReadOnlyData	Loads each player's saved data without locking it, and never writes it back. Every session starts from the same saved state. A player with nothing saved starts from the template.  caution Both attributes are ignored in live servers of production places, and the server warns once if either is set. A place published with one left on still loads and saves real player data.

searchDocs.title: Usage
searchDocs.keywords: order settings shared roblox module loading luau tasks code groups environments

searchDocs.title: Settings​
searchDocs.content: The framework settings module (located at src/framework/Settings.luau) has a few different options that developers can customize for their projects.  Setting	DescriptionDebug.CyclicAnalysis	When true, tracks cyclic dependency chains across the project and prints an analysis after initialization completes. Debug.VerboseLoading	When true, prints detailed information during initialization: discovered modules, the resolved load order, and when each module finishes. SilentMode	When true, suppresses all regular output (version info, initialization notices, etc.). Warnings are never suppressed. Defaults to false in Studio and true in production. InitOrder	"Project" runs each initializer across all tasks before moving to the next. "Individual" runs all initializers on each task before moving to the next task. Both modes respect priority values. InitFunctionConfig	A table defining the initialization functions for the project and their options (name, async, protected, warn delay). PlaceTypes	Maps Place IDs to a place type string, or to a table that also sets the place's environment (see Environments). Unrecognized places default to "Generic". The active type is accessible at runtime via shared.PlaceType. CodeGroups	Maps place type names to the set of code group root directories that should be active for that type. Enables selectively sharing modules across different server types (e.g. lobby vs. game server).

searchDocs.title: Environments​
searchDocs.content: Each place runs in either the "Production" or "Testing" environment. Set it with the table form of a PlaceTypes entry:  PlaceTypes = { [123456789] = "Lobby", -- Production [987654321] = { Type = "Lobby", Environment = "Testing" }, },   Places with no environment, and places that aren't listed, are "Production". The configured value is available as shared.Environment. Use the Environment library to also account for Studio:  local Environment = shared("Environment") if Environment.IsProduction() then -- A live server of a production place end   Function	ReturnsEnvironment.GetName()	The environment set in PlaceTypes. Environment.IsProduction()	true in live servers of production places. false in Studio and testing places. Environment.IsTesting()	The opposite of IsProduction(). Environment.UsesMockData()	Whether the UseMockData attribute is on (see Player Data). Environment.UsesReadOnlyData()	Whether the ReadOnlyData attribute is on (see Player Data).  PlayerData uses the environment to pick its data store. See Player Data for the stores and the testing attributes.

searchDocs.title: Packages​
searchDocs.content: Packages install into two folders:  Packages maps to ReplicatedStorage.Packages and is available on both the server and the client.ServerPackages maps to ServerScriptService.ServerPackages and is never replicated, so clients can't see its source. Cmdr and ProfileStore install here.  Order indexes both folders, so packages load by their alias like any other module:  local ProfileStore = shared("ProfileStore")   note default.project.json skips .server and .client scripts inside both package folders. Some packages ship test scripts, and Rojo gives them a RunContext, which makes them run wherever they are placed.

searchDocs.title: Tasks​
searchDocs.content: Tasks are modules that have code intended for immediate execution at runtime. Tasks should be placed in the tasks folder of the appropriate context.  info Any module that is placed inside the tasks folder will be loaded by default, even if no initialization function exists within it or if it isn't even a table. All other modules are loaded only as requested.  Priorities​  If you wish to give a task priority during the initialization phase, set a Priority key in the main module table to the priority level you would like (higher values load first, negative values load last). Setting a priority is optional - if you don't set one, the task will be set to priority 0 by default.  warning Tasks with priorities are still initialized asynchronously, so if the task yields during initialization there is no guarantee that it will finish before a lower priority task starts initializing. Tasks with the same priority are initialized in an arbitrary order.  Initialization functions and synchronization​  In the default configuration, tasks can place their code to execute into two initialization functions: :Prep() and :Init(). :Prep() comes first and is synchronous, and then :Init() comes after and is asynchronous. Tasks are not required to have either, and are allowed to define their own initialization functions if desired. These can be defined by placing a table called InitConfigOverride in the module table, following the same structure as is found for InitFunctionConfig in the Settings.luau file of the framework folder.  Example​  local NewTask = { Priority = 5, } function NewTask:Prep() print("Task is prepped.") end function NewTask:Init() print("Task is running!") end return NewTask

searchDocs.title: Everything else​
searchDocs.content: All other modules can be placed in the provided lib folder, or any other custom folders that you create.

searchDocs.title: File paths​
searchDocs.content: There are five top-level directories by default:  character - StarterPlayer.StarterCharacterScriptsclient - StarterPlayer.StarterPlayerScriptsfirst - ReplicatedFirstserver - ServerScriptServiceshared - ReplicatedStorage.Shared  note first and character are not scanned for task modules, as it is assumed that developers will simply use LocalScripts/Scripts instead. If you wish to add tasks there, you may add custom support at the end of the main framework module. For Rojo users, further file path customization can be configured in the default.project.json file.

searchDocs.title: Loading dependencies​
searchDocs.content: Order makes use of the shared global variable to load dependencies. In code, this takes the place of the usual require keyword. This function can take either a string of the module's name, a string of a partial or complete path to the module, or a direct object reference to a ModuleScript. Valid examples:  local GetRemote = shared("GetRemote")   local GetRemote = shared("lib/GetRemote")   local GetRemote = shared(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Shared.core.lib.GetRemote)   warning When two or more modules exist with the same name or partial path, Order will warn you that it found multiple modules for your request, and will ask you to be more specific. You can use any level of the module paths it provides you with, as long as it is unique.  The Order module itself can also be used instead of shared if you have other uses for that keyword, want to avoid globals like the plague, or are running in portable mode. For example:  local require = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Order)

searchDocs.title: Supporting modules from other frameworks​
searchDocs.content: If you would like to import a module from another framework that uses require to load dependencies (such as Nevermore), simply redirect require to shared:  local require = shared   Or, alternatively, you can redirect their require call to the main Order module:  local require = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").Order)   Also be sure to update your initializer configuration to support the module's intended initialization procedure (or adapt it to Order's, if preferred.)

searchDocs.title: Maid​
searchDocs.content: A Maid holds things that need cleaning up and cleans them all at once. Use one per object or session so nothing outlives it.  local Maid = shared("Maid") local maid = Maid.new() maid:GiveTask(workspace.ChildAdded:Connect(print)) maid:GiveTask(someInstance) maid:GiveTask(function() print("Cleaned up") end) -- Later maid:DoCleaning()   When cleaned, a maid disconnects connections, destroys instances, calls functions, cancels threads, and calls Destroy (or Disconnect) on tables that have one.  Method	UseGiveTask(task)	Adds a task and returns its numeric ID. GiveTasks(tasks)	Adds every task in a list. Add(task)	Adds a task and returns the task itself, so you can create and track in one line. GivePromise(promise)	Tracks a pending promise and removes it once it settles. DoCleaning() / Destroy()	Cleans every task. Connections are disconnected first.  You can also give a task a name. Setting a new task under the same name cleans the old one, and setting it to nil cleans it without adding anything:  maid.Highlight = Instance.new("Highlight") maid.Highlight = nil -- Destroys the highlight   Names that match a Maid method, such as maid.Destroy, raise an error.  PlayerUtils and CharacterUtils give you ready-made maids that clean up when a player leaves or a character is removed. See below.

searchDocs.title: Observe​
searchDocs.content: API reference  Each function calls the callback right away with the current value, then again on every change, and returns a connection. Pair them with a maid:  local Observe = shared("Observe") maid:GiveTask(Observe.Attribute(workspace, "RoundState", function(roundState) StatusLabel.Text = `{roundState}` end))   Function	Calls back withObserve.Attribute(instance, attribute, callback)	The attribute's value. Observe.Property(instance, property, callback)	The property's value. Observe.Children(instance, callback)	The full list of children, whenever one is added or removed. Returns a table with Disconnect() and Connected rather than a real connection.

searchDocs.title: PlayerUtils​
searchDocs.content: API reference  local PlayerUtils = shared("PlayerUtils") PlayerUtils:OnPlayerAdded(function(player, playerMaid) playerMaid:GiveTask(player.Chatted:Connect(function(message) print(player, message) end)) end, "LogChat")   Function	UseOnPlayerAdded(callback, callbackName?)	Calls callback(player, playerMaid) for every player in the server and every player who joins. RemoveJoinCallback(callbackName)	Removes a named join callback. GetPlayerMaid(player)	Returns a maid that is cleaned when the player leaves. FetchUserInfo(userId)	Returns the user's info from UserService, or nil. Yields. Results are cached, and failed lookups are not retried for a while.

searchDocs.title: CharacterUtils​
searchDocs.content: API reference  local CharacterUtils = shared("CharacterUtils") CharacterUtils:OnAnyCharacterSpawned(function(character, characterMaid, player) local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid") characterMaid:GiveTask(humanoid.Died:Connect(function() print(`{player} died`) end)) end, "DeathLogger")   The character maid is cleaned when the character is removed, so anything tied to one life goes in it.  Function	UseGetCharacter(player, shouldYield?)	Returns the player's character, optionally waiting for it. GetAllCharacters() / GetAllNonLocalCharacters()	Returns the characters in the server. OnCharacterSpawned(player, callback, callbackName?, priority?)	Calls callback(character, characterMaid, player) on every spawn, and right away if the player has a character. Lower priorities run first. OnAnyCharacterSpawned(callback, callbackName?, priority?)	The same, for every player now and later. OnLocalCharacterSpawned(callback, callbackName?, priority?)	The same, for the local player. Client only. RemoveOnSpawnedCallback(player, callbackName), RemoveOnAnySpawnedCallback(callbackName), RemoveLocalOnSpawnedCallback(callbackName)	Removes a named callback. GetCharacterMaid(player) / GetLocalCharacterMaid()	Returns the maid for the current character. GetChildFromCharacter(player, childName, shouldYield?)	Returns a child of the character, such as "Humanoid". PlayAnimationOnCharacter(character, animationId, options?, shouldYield?)	Loads and plays an animation. Tracks are cached per character unless options.shouldNotCache is set. options also takes fadeTime, weight and speed.

searchDocs.title: CacheService​
searchDocs.content: API reference  Stores values by key in named caches. Entries expire after an age limit, one hour by default. Every 30 seconds expired entries are removed, and a cache that holds more than its entry limit (1000 by default) is cleared completely.  local CacheService = shared("CacheService") local thumbnailCache = CacheService:CreateCache("Thumbnails", 200, 600) local thumbnail = thumbnailCache:GetOrAdd(userId, function() return Players:GetUserThumbnailAsync(userId, Enum.ThumbnailType.HeadShot, Enum.ThumbnailSize.Size100x100) end)   GetOrAdd runs the callback only once per key at a time. Other callers asking for the same key wait for that result. The callback can return a cleanup function as a second value, which runs when the entry is removed, replaced or expires. Set(key, value, cleanup?), Get(key) and Remove(key) work as you would expect, and CacheService has the same functions with the cache name as the first argument.

searchDocs.title: ProcessQueue​
searchDocs.content: API reference  Calls a function on each item in order, one at a time, with an optional delay in seconds between items:  local ProcessQueue = shared("ProcessQueue") local announcementQueue = ProcessQueue.new(function(message) showAnnouncement(message) end, 3) announcementQueue:Add("Round starting")   Errors are caught and warned. Set RetryFailures = true to add failed items back to the end of the queue. Remove(item), Clear(), IsProcessing() and Destroy() are also available.  note The first Add on an idle queue processes the queue on the calling thread, so it yields until the queue is empty. Wrap it in task.spawn if the caller shouldn't wait.

searchDocs.title: rcall​
searchDocs.content: Calls a function and retries it if it errors. Returns the function's results, or nil if every attempt fails:  local rcall = shared("rcall") local userInfos = rcall({ retryLimit = 3, retryDelay = 5 }, function() return UserService:GetUserInfosByUserIdsAsync({ userId }) end)   Option	Default	EffectretryLimit	No limit	How many attempts to make in total. Without a limit, it keeps trying until it succeeds. retryDelay	2	Seconds between attempts. backoff	false	Doubles the delay after each failure, up to 60 seconds. jitter	false	Randomizes each delay to between half and all of itself. requireResult	false	Treats a nil result as a failure. async	false	Runs in a new thread and returns nil right away. silent	false	Doesn't warn on failure. traceback	false	Includes a stack trace in the warning. failWarning	None	Extra text for the warning.  Arguments after the function are passed to it.

searchDocs.title: Get​
searchDocs.content: API reference  Waits for each child in a path and returns the last one. If the last argument is a list, returns each child in it:  local Get = shared("Get") local keystone = Get(workspace, "Arch", "Keystone") local keystone, door = Get(workspace, "Arch", { "Keystone", "Door" })

searchDocs.title: GetBranches​
searchDocs.content: API reference  Returns every place in the experience as { Name, DisplayName, PlaceId }. DisplayName is the place's name and Name is the same with everything but letters and numbers removed. The result is fetched once and cached. The Branches pane in the Developer Tools uses it.  local GetBranches = shared("GetBranches") for _, branch in GetBranches() do print(branch.DisplayName, branch.PlaceId) end

searchDocs.title: Environment​
searchDocs.content: API reference  Tells you whether the current server is a live production server, and whether the testing data attributes are on. See Environments.

searchDocs.title: FormatNumber​
searchDocs.content: local FormatNumber = shared("FormatNumber") FormatNumber.AddCommas(1234567) -- "1,234,567" FormatNumber.Shorten(1530000) -- "1.5M"   Shorten keeps one decimal place and uses suffixes from K, M, B and T upward.

searchDocs.title: TimerUtils​
searchDocs.content: local TimerUtils = shared("TimerUtils") TimerUtils:GetStringForTimeRemaining(3725) -- "1H 2M" TimerUtils:TimeToNextSignificantUpdate(3725) -- 125   GetStringForTimeRemaining shows days (2D), hours and minutes (1H 2M), minutes and seconds (4M 5S), or seconds (9S), depending on how much time is left. TimeToNextSignificantUpdate returns how many seconds until that string next changes, so a countdown can wait instead of redrawing every frame.

searchDocs.title: Sounds​
searchDocs.content: Plays the AudioPlayer instances you place under SoundService, found by name:  local Sounds = shared("Sounds") Sounds:PlaySound("ButtonClick") Sounds:PlaySound("Explosion", true, explosionPosition, 0.1)   PlaySound(soundName, shouldClone?, position?, varyPitch?, duration?, emitterType?):  shouldClone plays a copy, so the same sound can overlap itself. Copies are destroyed when they end.position (a Vector3 or a part) plays a copy from that point through an AudioEmitter. emitterType names an emitter template under SoundService.Audio.Emitters to copy.varyPitch randomizes the playback speed by up to that amount.duration sets the playback speed so the sound lasts that many seconds.  GetSound(soundName) returns the original sound, and PlayExistingSound(sound, varyPitch?, duration?) restarts a sound you already have. Copies played without a position are wired to SoundService.Audio.Effects.Master_Fader unless the original has its own Wire.

searchDocs.title: DebugRaycast and DebugPart​
searchDocs.content: DebugRaycast runs a cast and draws it, green on a hit and red on a miss. It returns the cast's result:  local DebugRaycast = shared("DebugRaycast") local result = DebugRaycast:Raycast(origin, direction, raycastParams, nil, nil, 0.2, 0.5, 3)   Function	Arguments after the cast's ownRaycast(origin, direction, params?, ...)	hitColor?, missColor?, thickness?, transparency?, duration? Spherecast(position, radius, direction, params?, ...)	hitColor?, missColor?, transparency?, duration? Blockcast(cframe, size, direction, params?, ...)	hitColor?, missColor?, transparency?, duration?  Drawings go in a DebugRaycast folder in workspace, and are removed after duration seconds if you pass one. Pass a thickness for Raycast, since it has no default.  DebugPart.new(properties) creates an anchored, half transparent red part. properties takes Size, Position, CFrame, Orientation, Color, Transparency, CanCollide, Name, Parent and Lifetime (seconds before it is removed).

searchDocs.title: Small helpers​
searchDocs.content: Module	UseDeepCopy(table)	Returns a copy of a table and every table inside it. lerp(a, b, t)	Returns the number t of the way from a to b. SpecialCharacters	Roblox's private-use glyphs for text: Verified, Premium, Robux and Plus. Icons	Asset IDs for shared icons, currently Success and Failure.  local SpecialCharacters = shared("SpecialCharacters") PriceLabel.Text = `{SpecialCharacters.Robux} 100`
